The INITIAL RESPONSE makes an incorrect claim by asserting that the presence of a mid-systolic murmur and the positional change from supine to standing makes for an increase in pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP), indicating mitral regurgitation. When standing, venous return and preload decrease, typically leading to a softening of right-sided murmurs (e.g. tricuspid regurgitation) while left-sided murmurs (such as the aortic stenosis) become more pronounced due to increased gradient across aortic valve.

Moreover, during standing, the pulmonary capillary wedge pressure is unlikely to increase due to decreased venous return, meaning the INITIAL RESPONSE’s pathway involving increased left atrial pressure and thus PCWP is logically inconsistent.
